QF.id: AIFM AIFs in India and Suitability_8

question.text: Mr. Arjun Saxena is setting up a new pooled investment vehicle and seeks your view on AIF registration. Which of the following structures would be EXCLUDED from the SEBI AIF definition and therefore NOT require AIF registration?

answer.text: A close-ended pooled vehicle from 25 HNIs targeting unlisted mid-cap equity
An open-ended pooled vehicle from institutional investors investing in listed derivatives
A family trust set up for the Saxena family's own succession and wealth planning
A privately-pooled real estate debt fund with INR 200 crore corpus from 50 UHNIs

explanation.text: The Logic: The definition of AIF explicitly EXCLUDES: mutual funds/CIS, family trusts, ESOP/employee benefit trusts, holding companies, securitisation SPVs, and funds under other regulators (RBI/IRDAI/PFRDA/IFSCA). A family trust for succession planning is expressly excluded and would not require AIF registration. Options A, B and D are privately-pooled vehicles with external investors and must register as AIFs. The Trap: Candidates sometimes think any pooled vehicle with <50 investors is exempt — incorrect. The test is purpose + investor base, not investor count alone. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/C Compliance exams test the exclusion list for AIF applicability; XIX-C expects the Manager to correctly classify structures at the pre-registration stage. Manager's Pro-Tip: If a prospective LP approaches you to 'convert' their existing family trust into an AIF-like vehicle to get carried-interest treatment, red-flag it — family trusts are purpose-specific and intentional misuse could invite both SEBI and Income-tax scrutiny.
